ideas.hypothesis: Ex-ante benefit-cost ratios of tramway projects rise mechanically when the appraisal's discount rate tracks falling market interest rates, so projects appraised in low-rate years are approved more often and have larger cost overruns relative to their appraised benefits. Reporting the full curve of approval probability across discount rates (a cost-effectiveness acceptability curve borrowed from trial design) will reorder the project ranking compared with a single fixed-rate appraisal.

sources.role: method: health-economic evaluation designed into the trial, the template for a pre-specified appraisal design
setting: a metropolitan plan with tram/rail construction financed through a consortium, giving a portfolio of appraised projects
mechanism: project success depends on how well the node is integrated, a benefit that is often left out of rate-sensitive appraisals
measure: trajectory-based service reliability as an ex-post benefit outcome
method caveat: data-quality pitfalls when big data are used to measure ex-post benefits

ideas.test: Collect published ex-ante appraisals (costs, benefit streams, discount rate used) for about 30-50 European tram projects from 2000-2019, plus each country's 10-year government bond yield in the appraisal year. Recompute each BCR at a common set of discount rates (1-7%), then regress approval/construction (and later the outturn/forecast cost ratio) on the discount rate used, controlling for city size and project length.
ideas.disconfirming: The discount rate used is unrelated to approval and to cost overruns once project characteristics are controlled, or the project rankings barely change across the range of discount rates.

ideas.hypothesis: Patient medical balances carry zero interest, so when consumer credit rates rise, patients put interest-bearing debts first and pay medical bills later. Practices' days in accounts receivable and bad-debt write-off ratios therefore rise with credit card interest rates, and the effect is strongest where consumer-driven (high-deductible) health plans are common.

sources.role: measure: unpaid balances, write-offs and refunds as practice-level outcomes
mechanism: consumer-driven health plans move payment responsibility to patients and put pressure on practice cash flow
finding: credit-control arrangements change both borrower behaviour and the amount of credit extended (a lender-side analogue)
method: a panel that splits incidents by type, applied here by splitting write-offs by payer and type
method: a systematic topic-trend review to locate gaps in research on consumer payment behaviour

ideas.test: Build a quarterly panel of practices' AR days and bad-debt ratios (from a practice-management benchmarking survey or a billing vendor), merged with the Federal Reserve credit card interest rate series and state-level high-deductible plan enrollment. Estimate fixed-effects regressions of AR days on the card rate, high-deductible penetration, and their interaction, separating the self-pay and insurer-paid parts of receivables.
ideas.disconfirming: The self-pay receivables of practices do not lengthen when card rates rise, or the response is no larger where high-deductible enrollment is high than where it is low.

ideas.hypothesis: Defaults are correlated, and the correlation is strongest during monetary tightening. Calibration tests that assume independent defaults therefore reject correctly calibrated rating grades much more often in years after policy-rate increases than in easing years, while one-factor (correlation-adjusted) tests show no such cyclical rejection pattern.

sources.role: method: approximate tests compared with simulation-based one-factor and multi-factor calibration tests under correlated defaults
measure: agency default and recovery statistics by rating grade
setting: a sovereign downgrade as an event that raises borrowing costs and clusters defaults
method: an acceptability-curve view, here reporting the probability of passing calibration as a function of the assumed asset correlation
method: revisiting a research agenda, used here to set priorities for validating rating models

ideas.test: Use annual default rates by rating grade from the published 1981-2019 agency default studies. For each grade-year, apply the binomial test and a one-factor Vasicek test, then regress the rejection indicators on the change in the policy rate over the prior 12-24 months.
ideas.disconfirming: The binomial test rejects no more often after tightening than after easing, or the one-factor test shows the same rate-linked rejection pattern.

ideas.hypothesis: When policy rates were near zero and real savings rates were negative, the response of homeownership to falling mortgage rates was weaker in high-foreclosure metros (Cuyahoga County/Cleveland, Orleans Parish) than in low-foreclosure metros. In the high-foreclosure metros, tighter lending and lost home equity sent households into renting.

sources.role: mechanism: near-zero target rates with negative real savings rates failed to raise growth and increased household debt
finding/setting: after the mortgage crisis, falling home values and tighter lending in Cuyahoga County moved households toward renting
setting: New Orleans as a comparison metro with distinctive post-shock policy and local institutions
setting: a mid-sized Rust Belt city (Syracuse) as an additional comparison metro
method: building an expected-price measure from CPS/MEPS microdata, here used for user cost of owning versus renting

ideas.test: County-year panel for 2000-2016 using ACS/decennial tenure shares, the Freddie Mac 30-year mortgage rate, county foreclosure rates and mortgage denial rates from HMDA. Estimate the homeownership-to-mortgage-rate elasticity before and during the zero-rate period, interacted with pre-crisis foreclosure intensity, and report Cuyahoga and Orleans as case counties.
ideas.disconfirming: The homeownership-rate elasticity during the zero-rate period is the same in high- and low-foreclosure counties, or tenure in high-foreclosure counties responds more to rate cuts, not less.

ideas.hypothesis: After Hurricane Katrina, building permit counts near New Orleans streetcar stops were less sensitive to lagged changes in interest rates than permit counts far from stops. The accessibility premium near fixed rail cushions developers against higher borrowing costs, so the permit-distance gradient steepens when rates rise.

sources.role: method/setting: post-Katrina permit frequency modelled by distance from streetcar stops with damage controls
mechanism/measure: the lagged Federal Funds rate is a significant driver of real-estate demand (lease renewals)
method: demand forecasting that combines perceived and empirical data
setting: international light-rail and streetcar developments for replication sites

ideas.test: Geocoded New Orleans building permits for 2005-2015, aggregated to block-group by quarter, with distance to the nearest streetcar stop, flood-damage share, and the lagged Fed Funds rate and 30-year mortgage rate. Fit a Poisson/negative binomial model with block-group fixed effects and a distance × lagged-rate interaction.
ideas.disconfirming: The distance × rate interaction is zero or positive, meaning permits near stops are at least as rate-sensitive as permits far from them.

ideas.hypothesis: Prices that regulators set on a cost-of-capital basis pass interest-rate changes through to customers with longer lags and less completely than deregulated prices. Studies that impose static or ad hoc specifications understate pass-through speed compared with general-to-specific dynamic models.

sources.role: setting/mechanism: easing restrictions on rate-setting and entry in trucking and rail
method: an argument for ambitious general-to-specific empirical modelling over restricted specifications
method: a systematic review of the statistical methods used to analyse an outcome, replicated here for pass-through studies
setting: a range of regulatory regimes (unregulated, hybrid, authority-led) for comparison
method: differing methodological traditions across fields studying the same relationship

ideas.test: (1) Systematically code published interest-rate pass-through studies for model specification and the speed of pass-through they report, then meta-regress the reported speed on specification type. (2) Using U.S. rail and truck freight price indices and Treasury yields from 1970-2000, estimate autoregressive distributed lag pass-through models before and after the 1980 deregulation.
ideas.disconfirming: Pass-through speed is no slower under regulation, and estimated speed does not differ systematically between static and dynamic specifications.

ideas.hypothesis: Once policy rates reached zero (2008-09), and again when central banks moved to negative rates (2014-16), central bank research agendas shifted measurably toward household balance sheets and debt. Topic shares changed after each date in an interrupted-time-series pattern, not as a gradual trend.

sources.role: finding: a central bank launched a new research effort on household balance sheets after the crisis
mechanism: near-zero rates increased household debt, making it a policy-relevant topic
method: revisiting an earlier research agenda item by item to measure progress
method: a structured statement of research and data needs as a template for coding agendas
mechanism: complexity and coordination problems that push research toward new topics

ideas.test: Collect titles and abstracts of Federal Reserve System and ECB working papers from 2000-2019. Classify topics with a dictionary or topic model (household debt, negative rates, forward guidance, and so on), then estimate segmented regressions of monthly topic shares with breaks at December 2008 and June 2014.
ideas.disconfirming: No significant level or slope change in the household-debt share at either break, or the shift comes before the policy events.

ideas.hypothesis: Tramway openings forecast in the trade press slip more often when long-term government borrowing rates were higher at the time of financing. Cities that publish a research-based plan before construction (systematically benchmarking good practice) slip less.

sources.role: measure: annual forecasts of new tramway openings worldwide
method: international benchmarking of recent public-transport implementations
method: bibliometric mapping of research on urban transit systems
method: content analysis of a research literature
method: a critique of case-study designs, guiding a comparative multi-city design

ideas.test: Content-analyse annual trade-press forecasts of new tram systems from 2000-2019 and record each system's actual opening date. Merge in the country's 10-year bond yield in the year construction started, plus an indicator for prior benchmarking or published planning studies, and estimate a duration model of delay.
ideas.disconfirming: Delay is unrelated to bond yields, or benchmarked or planned projects slip as much as the others.

ideas.hypothesis: Medical practices are more likely to adopt revenue-management tools borrowed from transport yield pricing (demand-based scheduling, prepayment discounts) when the cost of working capital (the prime rate) is high. Adopters' revenue per provider falls less during tightening periods than non-adopters'.

sources.role: method: yield-management pricing logic from rail ticketing
setting: practices seeking strategic ways to grow revenue
method: market research for understanding demand segments
measure: performance-based accountability metrics
method: analysing research trends and how research supply matches need

ideas.test: Repeated cross-section of practice benchmarking surveys (2005-2019) recording adoption of revenue-management practices and revenue per FTE physician, merged with the prime rate. Estimate an adoption logit on the lagged prime rate, then a difference-in-differences of revenue on adoption × tightening episodes.
ideas.disconfirming: Adoption does not rise with the prime rate, or adopters' revenue falls as much as non-adopters' during tightening.

ideas.hypothesis: Medical practices in areas with better transit access to jobs and services have shorter accounts-receivable cycles, because more patients attend in person and pay at the point of service. This advantage matters more when interest rates, and so the cost of carrying receivables, are high.

sources.role: measure: metro-level indicators of job access by transit
measure/mechanism: practice billing and point-of-service collection strategies

ideas.test: Merge practice-level AR days and no-show rates from a billing vendor or practice survey with tract-level transit accessibility scores and the prime rate. Regress AR days on accessibility and its interaction with the prime rate, controlling for payer mix and specialty.
ideas.disconfirming: Transit accessibility is unrelated to AR days or no-show rates, or the interaction with the prime rate is zero.
